decisions.title: Bounded AMQP 1.0 message mapping
decisions.section: Messages, Publish, Deliver, and AMQP 1.0 message format
decisions.issue: The Stream protocol transports AMQP 1.0 messages, but the public language-neutral model cannot preserve every AMQP section, identifier, annotation key, or application-property value safely.
interpretations: Expose the upstream AMQP message unchanged
Preserve one bounded mapping and reject unsupported representations
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned RabbitMQ Go client v1.8.3 supplies the AMQP 1.0 encoder used against RabbitMQ 4.3.5; no maintained RabbitMQ-supported PHP Streams client provides an independent non-Go differential decoder.
decisions.selected_behavior: Encode one AMQP 1.0 data section; map content type, message ID, correlation ID, creation time, the reserved routing annotation, string or binary annotations, and string or binary application properties; reject unsupported shapes and copy all received bytes.
decisions.rationale: An explicit bounded subset prevents silent coercion, aliasing, multiple-body ambiguity, and unbounded allocation while retaining opaque payloads.
decisions.security_consequences: Payload, key, value, and collection limits apply before application exposure, and rejected metadata is not rendered in errors.
decisions.resource_consequences: Exactly one bounded data section and bounded copied metadata are retained per message.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adding AMQP sections or value types, changing identifier normalization, or changing the reserved annotation requires compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Supported fields retain their AMQP 1.0 meaning without string coercion; unsupported or multiple data sections fail closed.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ defines Stream framing and AMQP 1.0 message payloads; the smaller public mapping is adapter policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported peer or application requires another AMQP 1.0 representation with deterministic bounded semantics.

decisions.title: Confirmation ambiguity and publishing identity remain explicit
decisions.section: Publish, Publish Confirm, Publish Error, and Query Publisher Sequence
decisions.issue: A client can lose the connection after publication admission but before observing Publish Confirm or Publish Error, and named-producer publishing IDs do not define application-wide exactly-once processing.
interpretations: Treat every local failure as not sent
Preserve definite, rejected, and ambiguous outcomes and scope deduplication to one producer name and stream
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ 4.3.5 confirms accepted publications and the pinned Go client exposes publishing IDs, but neither can recover an unobserved terminal response after connection loss.
decisions.selected_behavior: Report not sent only before transport admission; map positive confirmation and publish error exactly; complete every admitted publication without a definitive response as ambiguous; never invisibly retry it; and require one named producer owner for monotonic publishing IDs.
decisions.rationale: Calling an uncertain send absent can duplicate retained data, while calling stream-scoped deduplication exactly once overstates its boundary.
decisions.security_consequences: Confirmation errors and publishing identities remain bounded and payload-free in diagnostics.
decisions.resource_consequences: Outstanding confirmations are bounded and each admission reaches exactly one terminal callback during failure or close.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must reconcile ambiguous results and preserve producer-name ownership when using deduplication.
decisions.wire_consequences: The adapter uses RabbitMQ publishing IDs and confirmation frames without compensating frames or automatic duplicate publication.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ documents confirmation and publisher-sequence operations but no recovery operation for a response lost with the connection.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ adds an authoritative per-publication outcome query or changes publishing-ID scope.

decisions.title: Named offsets advance only after successful handling
decisions.issue: The protocol stores named offsets independently from application side effects and does not determine whether applications store before or after processing.
interpretations: Store only the successfully handled contiguous partition position
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ clients expose offset store and query primitives while leaving application handler timing and external side-effect ownership to the caller.
decisions.selected_behavior: Resolve stored starts through Query Offset, process each backing stream sequentially, and Store Offset only after successful handler policy; a failed or ambiguous store preserves at-least-once redelivery.
decisions.rationale: Storing before success can lose work, whereas storing after success exposes the unavoidable duplicate window explicitly.
decisions.security_consequences: Consumer names and offsets are validated and broker failures are reduced to stable categories.
decisions.resource_consequences: Partition workers, handler duration, store cadence, retries, and reconnect work remain bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Handlers must be idempotent because external effects and broker offsets are not atomic.
decisions.wire_consequences: Named Query Offset and Store Offset commands are separate from message delivery and external effects.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ defines named offset storage and lookup but not application transaction composition.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ introduces an atomic handler-effect and offset protocol usable through the supported client.

decisions.title: Replay fails closed across retention and start-position clamping
decisions.section: Offset Tracking, Data Retention, and Consuming
decisions.issue: RabbitMQ may clamp unavailable offset or timestamp subscriptions to retained data, so a successful subscription does not prove that the requested exact historical range exists.
interpretations: Snapshot retained bounds and reject every unavailable or changed exact range
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ 4.3.5 exposes retained first and last positions and clamps some subscription starts; ordinary clients can accept that behavior without an exact replay contract.
decisions.selected_behavior: Replay uses an isolated unnamed cursor, stores no offset, snapshots exact retained bounds, rejects removed starts and unavailable ends, and accepts only messages inside the requested inclusive range and unchanged ordered topology.
decisions.rationale: Failing closed distinguishes exact audit replay from best-effort catch-up and prevents silent history gaps.
decisions.security_consequences: Replay requires explicit side-effect policy and exposes no payload in range diagnostics.
decisions.resource_consequences: Range size, buffered messages, cursor lifetime, topology size, and broker operations are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Requests that RabbitMQ could clamp successfully may instead return a retention or range error.
decisions.wire_consequences: The adapter issues ordinary metadata and subscription commands but rejects deliveries outside the preflighted exact range.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ documents offset specifications and retention; exact bounded replay is adapter policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ adds an authoritative exact-range replay operation with explicit gap reporting.

decisions.title: Super Stream topology owns routing and partition-local order
decisions.section: Super Streams, Routing, and Single Active Consumer
decisions.issue: A Super Stream is an ordered set of backing streams, and topology or routing changes can remap keys without creating global order.
interpretations: Treat a Super Stream as one globally ordered log
Delegate arbitrary routing to raw client options
Pin ordered topology and use one explicit stable hash policy with partition-local ordering
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ's supported clients expose Super Stream routing strategies, but cross-language hash compatibility depends on every client selecting the same algorithm and partition order.
decisions.selected_behavior: Discover and validate one exact ordered backing-stream topology, hash each explicit routing key with the selected client-compatible strategy, keep each partition sequential, and reject missing, duplicate, oversized, or changed topology.
decisions.rationale: Making topology and hash policy visible preserves per-key partition affinity without inventing global ordering.
decisions.security_consequences: Routing keys and topology identities are bounded and not exposed through payload-bearing diagnostics.
decisions.resource_consequences: Partition count, topology queries, sessions, workers, and routing work are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adding, removing, or reordering partitions and changing the hash strategy are migration decisions that can remap keys.
decisions.wire_consequences: Publications target one backing stream; ordering exists only within that stream, not across the Super Stream.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ defines Super Streams and routing strategies; topology pinning and compatibility review are adapter policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ standardizes a versioned cross-client routing algorithm or global-order primitive.

decisions.title: Verified TLS and bounded authentication are the production transport
decisions.section: Connection, Peer Properties, SASL Handshake, SASL Authenticate, and Tune
decisions.issue: The protocol supports authentication over plain or TLS transports, but transport verification, credential lifetime, endpoint failover, and production plaintext policy are application choices.
interpretations: Default to plaintext and static credentials
Require verified TLS in production and bounded caller-owned credentials and endpoints
decisions.peer_behavior: RabbitMQ clients permit plaintext and TLS configurations; the live RabbitMQ 4.3.5 provider accepts verified TLS and mTLS and rejects invalid identity, authentication, and authorization.
decisions.selected_behavior: Default to verified TLS 1.2 or newer, reject InsecureSkipVerify, require an explicit development-only plaintext policy, clone caller TLS state, resolve bounded credentials for each environment, and classify authentication and authorization separately.
decisions.rationale: Safe production defaults prevent credential disclosure and hostname bypass while allowing deliberate local development and rotation.
decisions.security_consequences: Hostname verification, trusted roots, optional mTLS, least-privilege credentials, and payload-free errors remain mandatory production boundaries.
decisions.resource_consequences: Credential size, provider duration, endpoints, connection attempts, RPC time, backoff, and opened resources are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Plaintext requires explicit development policy, and raw client options cannot weaken transport or lifetime rules.
decisions.wire_consequences: Production connections negotiate RabbitMQ Streams over verified TLS and SASL with the configured bounded identity.
decisions.upstream_status: RabbitMQ defines connection and SASL exchanges; verified transport and bounded credential policy remain adapter and root policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: RabbitMQ changes supported SASL or TLS requirements or the selected client exposes a safer bounded transport primitive.
